{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |CoachRank= |APRank= |mode=Basketball |year=2016–17 |team=New Mexico State Aggies |image=New Mexico State Aggies wordmark.svg |image_size=250 |conference=Western Athletic Conference |division= |short_conf=WAC |record=28–6 |conf_record=11–3 |head_coach=[[Paul Weir (basketball)|Paul Weir]] |hc_year = 1st |asst_coach1=Jesse Bopp |asst_coach2=[[Aerick Sanders]] |asst_coach3=Marc Hsu |asst_coach4= |stadium=[[Pan American Center]] |champion=[[2017 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]] champions |bowl=[[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = First Round }} {{2016–17 WAC men's basketball standings}} The '''2016–17 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team''' represented [[New Mexico State University]] during the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Aggies, led by first-year head coach [[Paul Weir (basketball)|Paul Weir]], played their home games at the [[Pan American Center]] in [[Las Cruces, New Mexico]] as members of the [[Western Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 28–6, 11–3 in WAC play to finish in a tie for second place. They defeated [[2016–17 Chicago State Cougars men's basketball team|Chicago State]], [[2016–17 UMKC Kangaroos men's basketball team|UMKC]], and [[2016–17 Cal State Bakersfield Roadrunners men's basketball team|Cal State Bakersfield]] to win the [[2017 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]]. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2016–17 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]]. On April 11, 2017, head coach Paul Weir resigned to become the head coach at [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2017-04-11/college-basketball-new-mexico-hires-nmsus-paul-weir-head|title=New Mexico hires NMSU's Paul Weir as new head coach | NCAA.com|website=www.ncaa.com}} On April 17, the school hired [[Chris Jans]] as head coach.{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/new-mexico-state-hires-wichita-state-assistant-chris-jans-to-replace-paul-weir/|title=New Mexico State hires Wichita State assistant Chris Jans to replace Paul Weir|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-06-28|language=en}} == Previous season == The [[2015–16 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|Aggies]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] 23–11, 13–1 in WAC play to win the WAC regular season championship. They defeated [[2015–16 UMKC Kangaroos men's basketball team|UMKC]] to advance to the championship game of the [[2016 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]] where they lost to [[2015–16 Cal State Bakersfield Roadrunners men's basketball team|Cal State Bakersfield]]. As a regular season conference champion who failed to win their conference tournament, they received an automatic bid to the [[2016 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2015–16 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team|Saint Mary's]]. On April 16, 2016, head coach [[Marvin Menzies]] left the school to accept the head coaching position at [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/nmsu/2016/04/16/reports-unlv-menzies-agree-deal-new-rebels-head-coach/83123820/|title=NMSU BASKETBALL: Marvin Menzies hired as new UNLV head coach|newspaper=Las Cruces Sun-News|access-date=2017-02-09|language=en}} On April 26, the school hired Paul Weir, an assistant coach under Menzies, as head coach.{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/paul-weir-promoted-as-new-mexico-states-next-head-coach/|title=Paul Weir promoted as New Mexico State's next head coach|newspaper=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-02-09|language=en}} ==Departures== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
